rubrics.justification: The model appropriately stated that no image was available to it and did not fabricate embryo-specific morphology. However, it therefore provided no actual morphological assessment of the visible embryo.
It integrated most relevant factors well, including age, BMI, PCOS, ovarian reserve, sperm quality, endometrium, prior cycle, and transfer day, and linked them to prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and generally consistent, with probability ranges tied to embryo quality and patient factors. Minor issues include overemphasis on a single prior failed cycle and some speculative explanations.

Most recommendations are broadly evidence-based (single embryo transfer, luteal support, uterine cavity review), but suggesting ERA/EMMA/ALICE and especially strongly recommending PGT-A after one failed cycle in a 28-year-old is more aggressive than guideline-supported practice.
The response gives practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, though some recommendations are somewhat generic and a few are not ideally prioritized for this prognosis group.
